verdict.rationale: Discord documents its own credential types: per-app bot tokens and OAuth2 bearer tokens from a registered developer application. The OAuth2 page describes a grant that limits access to a specific resource (`/users/@me/connections`), which implies scoped tokens, but least-privilege scoping and bot permission controls are not spelled out. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the OAuth2 scope list and least-privilege design, bot permission or intent restrictions on bot tokens, agent-specific credential issuance and revocation, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Authenticating with the Discord API can be done in one of two ways: 1. Using a bot token... 2. Using an OAuth2 bearer token
The first step in implementing OAuth2 is registering a developer application and retrieving your client ID and client secret.
